quests.instruction: Which 2D shape do you get if you look straight down at the flat top of a cylinder, the flat base of a cone, AND the widest cross-section of a sphere, all at once?
quests.hint: All three of these solid shapes share the very same flat 2D shape somewhere on their surface.
quests.explanation: A cylinder's flat top, a cone's flat base, and a sphere's widest slice are all circles.
quests.funFact: The circle is the one flat shape that connects three very different solid shapes.

quests.instruction: Which shape matches a stop sign, having exactly as many lines of symmetry as it has sides — 8 of each?
quests.hint: For a regular shape, the lines of symmetry always equal the number of sides — think of the stop-sign shape.
quests.explanation: A stop sign is an octagon, with exactly 8 sides and 8 lines of symmetry.
quests.funFact: An octagon's symmetry and its side count are simply two ways of describing the same balanced shape.

quests.instruction: Which shape is the simplest possible polygon, has the fewest lines of symmetry among the regular polygons in this game, and is also used to build both pyramids and hexagons?
quests.hint: Think of the 3-sided shape that shows up as a building block for so many other shapes.
quests.explanation: A triangle is the simplest polygon, has only 3 lines of symmetry among regular polygons, and helps build both pyramids and hexagons.
quests.funFact: Triangles are often called the building blocks of geometry because so many other shapes can be made from them.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape do you get by stretching a cube longer in just one direction, without changing the other two?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape that is a cube's stretched-out relative.
quests.explanation: Stretching a cube longer in just one direction turns it into a rectangular prism.
quests.funFact: This is the same relationship a square has with a rectangle, but one dimension higher, in 3D.

quests.instruction: Which shape shares a square's 4 equal sides and 4 lines of symmetry, but is traditionally drawn balancing on a single bottom point?
quests.hint: Think back to the shape that is really just a square, tipped over to stand on its corner.
quests.explanation: A diamond shares a square's 4 equal sides and 4 lines of symmetry, but is drawn balancing on one point instead of a flat edge.
quests.funFact: Every property a square has, a diamond has too — only the way it's drawn is different.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape is the only one in this whole game with zero flat faces, zero straight edges, and zero sharp corners?
quests.hint: Think of the roundest, smoothest solid shape you've learned, with nothing flat or pointed anywhere.
quests.explanation: A sphere is the only solid shape here with zero flat faces, zero edges, and zero corners.
quests.funFact: Every other solid shape in this game has at least one flat face or one sharp point.

quests.instruction: Home plate, a classic house outline, and the shape hidden at the center of a 5-pointed star all share which shape?
quests.hint: Think of the 5-sided shape that connects a baseball field, a house drawing, and a star all at once.
quests.explanation: Home plate, a house outline, and the hidden center of a star are all shaped like a pentagon.
quests.funFact: Once you learn to spot a pentagon, you'll notice it hiding in more places than you'd expect.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has 8 corners where exactly 3 square faces meet, 12 equal edges, and 6 equal square faces, all at the same time?
quests.hint: Think of the single most balanced solid shape you've learned, with every measurement matching.
quests.explanation: A cube has all of these properties at once: 8 corners, 12 equal edges, and 6 equal square faces.
quests.funFact: No other solid shape in this game matches a cube's perfect balance in every single measurement.

quests.instruction: Which shape can tile a floor with zero gaps, has 6 lines of symmetry, and matches both honeycomb cells and some pencil edges?
quests.hint: Think of the 6-sided shape that connects bees, pencils, and perfect floor tiling all at once.
quests.explanation: A hexagon fits all three clues: it tiles with no gaps, has 6 lines of symmetry, and matches honeycomb and pencil shapes.
quests.funFact: Very few shapes can claim all three of these properties together.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has exactly 1 corner, exactly 1 curved edge, exactly 1 flat face, and exactly 1 curved surface?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape with the smallest possible count of everything — just one of each part.
quests.explanation: A cone has exactly one of each: one corner, one curved edge, one flat face, and one curved surface.
quests.funFact: No other solid shape in this game has such a simple, matching count of just one for every feature.

quests.instruction: Which shape, when you fold it corner to corner, always creates two identical right triangles, no matter which of its two corner-to-corner lines you choose?
quests.hint: Think of the shape where both diagonal folds always create perfectly matching triangle halves.
quests.explanation: A square's 4 equal sides mean that either diagonal fold always creates two identical right triangles.
quests.funFact: A plain rectangle's diagonal fold also makes two triangles, but they only match perfectly like this in a square.

quests.instruction: Which shape do you get by slicing all 4 corners off a square, then checking that you now have 8 total sides?
quests.hint: A square has 4 sides — slicing off all 4 corners adds exactly 4 more.
quests.explanation: Slicing all 4 corners off a square adds 4 new sides to its original 4, giving 8 total sides, just like an octagon.
quests.funFact: This corner-slicing trick is a hands-on way to see exactly where an octagon's extra sides come from.

quests.instruction: Which shape is hiding inside a slice of pizza, a folded sandwich corner, AND half of a diagonally cut square, all three at once?
quests.hint: Think of the 3-sided shape shared by a pizza slice, a sandwich corner, and half a square.
quests.explanation: A pizza slice, a folded sandwich corner, and half of a diagonally cut square are all triangles.
quests.funFact: The same simple 3-sided shape connects food, folding, and geometry all at once.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape would look identical in a photograph no matter which direction the camera pointed at it?
quests.hint: Think of the one solid shape with a surface that never changes no matter the viewing angle.
quests.explanation: A sphere looks exactly the same from every possible camera angle, since its surface never changes shape.
quests.funFact: Even a cylinder or cube would look different from different angles, but a sphere never does.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 5 lines of symmetry, 5 equal sides, and connects a baseball field's home plate to a school crossing sign?
quests.hint: Think of the 5-sided shape shared by a sports field marking and a road safety sign.
quests.explanation: A pentagon connects all three clues: 5 lines of symmetry, 5 equal sides, home plate, and school crossing signs.
quests.funFact: Real-world designers often reuse the same simple shapes for very different purposes.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape do a cereal box, a book, and a brick all share, even though none of them are perfect cubes?
quests.hint: Think of the box-shaped solid that doesn't require every side to be equal, unlike a cube.
quests.explanation: A cereal box, a book, and a brick are all rectangular prisms, since their sides don't need to be equal like a cube's.
quests.funFact: Only a very specific rectangular prism, with every side matching, would count as a cube.

quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly 2 more sides than a pentagon and exactly 2 fewer sides than an octagon?
quests.hint: Start from a pentagon's 5 sides and count forward by 2.
quests.explanation: A hexagon's 6 sides sit exactly 2 more than a pentagon's 5 and 2 fewer than an octagon's 8.
quests.funFact: This kind of side-counting shows exactly how neighboring polygons relate to each other.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape, when you trace just one of its faces, always gives you the same flat shape as tracing any of its other 5 faces?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape where every single face is identical, unlike a rectangular prism.
quests.explanation: Every face of a cube is an identical square, so tracing any one of its 6 faces always gives the same result.
quests.funFact: A rectangular prism might have different-shaped faces, but a cube's faces are always exactly the same.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 5 points, 5 lines of symmetry, and a hidden pentagon at its very center?
quests.hint: Think of the pointy shape that shares its symmetry count with a pentagon, since one hides inside the other.
quests.explanation: A star has 5 points, 5 lines of symmetry, and a pentagon hiding right at its center.
quests.funFact: You've now learned how closely a star and a pentagon are related to each other.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has 2 flat circle faces, 2 curved edges, zero corners, and one curved surface connecting the top to the bottom?
quests.hint: Think of the tube-like solid shape with round ends but no sharp points anywhere.
quests.explanation: A cylinder has exactly 2 flat circle faces, 2 curved edges, zero corners, and one curved connecting surface.
quests.funFact: Counting up all these features is a thorough way to be completely sure a shape is a cylinder.

quests.instruction: Which shape is a rectangle, a rhombus, AND the only regular quadrilateral, all names describing the very same shape?
quests.hint: Think of the one 4-sided shape balanced enough to earn all three of these names at once.
quests.explanation: A square fits all three descriptions: it's a special rectangle, a special rhombus, and the only regular quadrilateral.
quests.funFact: Shapes can sometimes belong to more than one family at the same time, just like a square does.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has a polygon base, triangle faces leaning inward, and narrows to exactly one single top point, unlike a prism?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape whose sides always lean inward toward one peak, unlike a straight-sided prism.
quests.explanation: Unlike a prism, whose sides go straight up, a pyramid's triangle faces lean inward to meet at one single peak.
quests.funFact: This inward lean is exactly what gives every pyramid its pointed, triangular silhouette.

quests.instruction: Which shape ranks highest in side count, corner count, AND lines of symmetry among every 2D shape you've studied in this entire game?
quests.hint: Think of the many-sided shape used for stop signs, which beats every other named polygon here.
quests.explanation: With 8 sides, 8 corners, and 8 lines of symmetry, the octagon ranks highest among all the named polygons in this game.
quests.funFact: Only a circle, with its infinite symmetry, ultimately beats an octagon — but a circle has no sides or corners to count at all.

quests.instruction: Which shape has no sides, no corners, and infinite lines of symmetry, making it the single most balanced shape in this entire game?
quests.hint: Think of the one shape that beats every polygon, no matter how many sides that polygon has.
quests.explanation: A circle has no sides, no corners, and infinite lines of symmetry, making it the most balanced shape you've studied.
quests.funFact: You've now completed a journey from a simple circle all the way to a full understanding of shapes, sides, solids, and symmetry.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has infinite lines of symmetry running through its center, just like a circle does in 2D?
quests.hint: Think of the solid, 3D version of a circle's endless symmetry.
quests.explanation: A sphere has infinite lines of symmetry running through its center, just like a circle does in two dimensions.
quests.funFact: This makes a sphere the 3D version of a circle's perfectly balanced symmetry.

quests.instruction: Which shape can combine with itself to build a square, a diamond, a hexagon, and even a pyramid, more than any other shape in this game?
quests.hint: Think of the simplest possible polygon, used again and again to build so many other shapes.
quests.explanation: A triangle can combine with itself to build a square, a diamond, a hexagon, and a pyramid — more than any other shape here.
quests.funFact: This is exactly why triangles are often called the true building blocks of geometry.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape is the meeting point of a square (its face), a rectangular prism (its family), and perfect 3D balance (its defining trait)?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape whose every face is a square, and whose every measurement matches perfectly.
quests.explanation: A cube's faces are squares, it belongs to the rectangular prism family, and its perfect balance defines it.
quests.funFact: Very few shapes connect this many ideas from across the whole game the way a cube does.

quests.instruction: After everything you've learned about sides, corners, solids, and symmetry, which single shape still stands alone with no sides, no corners, and endless symmetry?
quests.hint: Think all the way back to one of the very first shapes you ever learned in this game.
quests.explanation: After every lesson in this game, the circle still stands alone: no sides, no corners, and endless symmetry.
quests.funFact: Congratulations on completing a full journey through shapes, from the simplest circle to the most advanced reasoning!

quests.instruction: Which solid shape ties together a flat polygon base, triangle faces, ancient monuments, and a single meeting point at the top?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape whose every triangle face rises to meet at exactly one peak.
quests.explanation: A pyramid ties all of these together: a flat base, triangle faces, ancient monuments, and one peak where every face meets.
quests.funFact: You've now mastered how a pyramid connects flat 2D triangles into one complete solid shape.

quests.instruction: As a final challenge: which shape has 6 sides, 6 corners, 6 lines of symmetry, tiles perfectly with no gaps, and is built from 6 triangles at once?
quests.hint: Think of the honeycomb-inspired shape that ties together sides, symmetry, tiling, and triangles all in one.
quests.explanation: A hexagon ties together every one of these clues: 6 sides, 6 corners, 6 lines of symmetry, perfect tiling, and 6 triangle wedges.
quests.funFact: You've reached the end of the Shapes journey — congratulations on mastering every shape from circle to hexagon and beyond!
